name: cudnn_grid_sampler
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI): aten::cudnn_grid_sampler(Tensor self, Tensor grid) -> Tensor output. Registered schemas: aten::cudnn_grid_sampler(Tensor self, Tensor grid) -> Tensor output; aten::cudnn_grid_sampler.out(Tensor self, Tensor grid, *, Tensor(a!) out) -> Tensor(a!). The original Gems pytest owns the full contract, including overloads, keyword arguments, returns, errors, aliasing and mutation; do not narrow tests to this signature. Semantics: sampling of a rank-4 input (N, C, H, W) at normalized (x, y) coordinates carried by grid (N, Hg, Wg, 2), producing output (N, C, Hg, Wg); grid.size(-1) must be 2 and grid.size(0) must equal input.size(0). Coordinates inside [-1, 1] sample real pixels; coordinates on or beyond the border are native-valid, and whether a sample keeps any edge weight there is decided by the native kernel, so every case is compared against the native result and no zero fill is assumed for any coordinate. Non-finite coordinates are also native-valid: on the backend where this was measured the affected samples come back as NaN instead of raising, and NaN matching is left to the shared comparison helper. Operand dtypes are limited to the floating set float32/float16, plus float64 when the device reports float64 support; on the backend where the rejection behaviour was measured (vendor "nvidia"), other operand dtypes and mismatched input/grid dtypes raise. Invalid shapes raise one of RuntimeError/TypeError/IndexError — a grid whose last dimension is not 2, non-rank-4 operands, batch mismatch, and 0-dim operands, with the 0-dim form documented as the case that surfaces IndexError. Non-contiguous operands and non-zero storage offsets are exercised and compared against the native result, and the operator is differentiable with respect to both input and grid. Overload-dependent behaviour: the .out overload is invoked as cudnn_grid_sampler(inp, grid, out=buf), where the required keyword-only out buffer is mutated and aliased, and the call returns that same buffer object; the representative default overload listed here neither mutates nor aliases any parameter.
